# ADR 0003: No reference execution; the project finishes on the Linux workstation

## Decision and authority

Adopted by user direction on 2026-10-18: "mac observation not possible; we are
finishing the proj on this x86 machine". No macOS host is available. Neither
Mach-O slice of the reference build can run on the Linux x86_64 workstation, and
no compatibility layer is authorized. All remaining analysis, specification,
handoff, implementation and validation work happens on this workstation.

This decision narrows [ADR 0002](adr-0002-static-first-analysis.md). Static
evidence becomes the only source of reference behavior. That evidence is the
decompiled arm64 and x86_64 corpora, shipped resources, schemas, scripts and
saved documents, and published documentation.

## Extracted execution of original code

Amended by user direction on 2026-10-18: "integration test style observation is
still possible if you can compile portions of the original program on this
machine". The whole application cannot run here, but some of its own machine code can.

- **What is permitted.** The x86_64 slice can be loaded into a harness process on this
  host, and self-contained functions can be called with recorded inputs. macOS
  x86_64 and Linux x86_64 share the System V AMD64 calling convention. Execution of
  the shipped bytes counts as reference evidence of a new kind, labelled X
  (extracted execution).
- **What it shows.** It shows what the original code computes for the given
  inputs. It does not show how the application reaches that code, what state
  it holds there, or what the user sees. The harness supplies the setup, and
  every stub or replaced import is recorded with the result.
- **Slice.** Results bind to the x86_64 slice. The release target is the arm64
  slice, so arm64 equivalence is an inference. It must be checked by comparing the
  two slices' code statically, and noted wherever floating-point evaluation could
  differ (for example, fused multiply-add on arm64).
- **Recompiled decompiler output** is a static derivation, not X evidence,
  unless it is checked against X runs of the same function.
- **Tooling.** Only tools already installed are used (gcc, gdb, objdump). Adding an
  emulator for the arm64 slice needs separate user approval.

## Consequences

- **Runtime escalation.** ADR 0002's escalation rule has no whole-application
  path. A question that would have needed observation is answered by
  extracted execution where the behavior lives in a self-contained function.
  Otherwise it is answered statically or stays unknown. Unknown behavior is excluded from releases, never guessed.
- **Phase 4 probes.** The [probe batch](../research/phase4-probe-batch.md) will
  not run as planned. It is kept as the record of what observation would have
  settled. Each probe's question becomes an extracted-execution target, a
  static investigation target or a permanent unknown.
- **Specs.** A clause or case that waits on a probe stays unknown or ungraded
  and cites this decision. A static derivation stays labelled static. Neither
  is ever relabelled as observed.
- **Releases.** Released payloads are not rewritten. Their "comparison not-run"
  obligations are now permanent: no original-versus-candidate comparison will
  happen. Extracted-execution results may support a later release revision.
- **Verification.** Candidate checks compare against released expectations, which are
  static-derived or, where available, from extracted execution. Reports must say so and must not claim compatibility with
  Live. Where coverage would show a reference comparison, it records it as
  unavailable.
- **Implementation.** The candidate is built and tested on this Linux x86_64
  workstation. Clean-room separation still applies (ADR 0001, AGENTS.md).
  Implementation needs a separately restricted workspace with only released
  handoffs and neutral governance. This decision does not provision one.

# Corpus device: signal chain and resonator (decompiled)

**Question.** What does Live 12.4.3's bundled Corpus audio effect compute, from
Live's parameter call down to each output sample? The original 2026-10-17
report below used decompiled bundle evidence only. Later bounded x86 extracted
execution belongs to [device DSP evidence](device-dsp-extracted.md); neither
the original application nor the arm64 device has been executed.

**Answer.**
- **Engine.** Corpus is a small modular engine of linked per-channel modules
  (*Inferred:* Applied Acoustics–style, from the module and class names).
- **Signal path.** The input splits into dry and wet through a panpot. The wet
  part goes through a clean gain (Live's Drive) and a band filter into one
  `ab_resonator` per channel. The resonator outputs pass a width crossfade, and
  the dry signal is added back.
- **Resonator models.** Five body types are banks of two-pole modal filters
  with fixed mode-ratio tables. Pipe and Tube are two-line waveguides.
- **Pitch.** Pitch arrives in octaves around 261.62 Hz from a pitch hub, which
  adds the LFO and Detune.
- **Parameters.** Live sends 38 numbered parameters, and the device uses the
  first 37. Resonator values are
  quantized to 128 controller steps.

Live's side is traced in the [device parameter mapping](device-parameter-mapping-native.md)
(N5). It confirms the Live names for host indices 0–36 below. Current conversion
claims belong to [Corpus requirement002](../specs/device-corpus.md#req-device-corpus-002--from-stored-values-to-host-values),
including its unaccepted position assumption A1; the historical report does not
establish a general stored-value identity. The [reviewed position companion](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/reviews/corpus-position-value-source-review.json)
resolves conditional initialization/pull/conversion only, with actual emission
and the public parameter path still unknown.

## Host parameters

`_SetParameterA` calls the wrapper at `0xd75c`. That function converts the host
value *v* to a controller value *c* in 0–127 and sends it to a module. The
constructor at `0xc40c` builds the 37-entry routing table. The module drivers
map *c* to a value:

| Driver | Mapping |
| --- | --- |
| Linear | *c* = 64 gives the midpoint, otherwise *c*/127 |
| Exponential | min·(max/min)^(*c*/127) |
| Cubic | (*c*/127)³, with 0.125 at *c* = 64 |
| Integer | Controller 64 gives 63 |

The resonator's handler (`0x20fc8`) truncates every value to an integer
controller.

The conversions in the table:
- **D:** `v ≤ 0.5 ? 128v : 126v+1`
- **B:** `v < 0 ? 63.5v+63.5 : 63v+64`
- **P:** `64 + 31.5v`

| Host | Live parameter (confirmed by N5) | Target | Conversion → value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | ResonanceType | resonator type | table `0x2a450` = [1,2,3,4,5,7,6] |
| 1 | Decay | resonator decay | D → 0.05·700^(c/127) s |
| 2 | FreqDamping | resonator tone | B, −1…1 |
| 3 | Inharmonics | resonator inharmonicity | B, −1…1 |
| 4 | Ratio | resonator ratio | D → 1…20 (exp) |
| 5 | Radius | resonator tube_radius | inverted D → 0.005…0.4 (exp) |
| 6 | Frequency | hub fixed pitch | D → −4…+4 octaves, 1 ms ramp |
| 7 | Transpose | hub transpose | `int(v)+48`, MIDI pitch mode only |
| 8 | FineTranspose | hub fine | `1.27v+63.5` → ±0.5 semitone, MIDI pitch mode only |
| 9 | Detune | hub detune | B → ±1/12 octave, opposite sign per channel |
| 10 | PitchBendRange | hub bend range | integer, 0–24 semitones |
| 11 | AmpFreq | resonator amp_freq | B, −1…1 |

MidiMode is sent as host index 37 and ignored, because the device's default
path accepts only indices below 37 (N5). Several mappings fit Live's stored
ranges exactly: the bipolar parameters, Transpose ±48, Fine ±50, BandWidth
0.5–9 and the phase angles 0–360. N5 confirms that Live passes those values
through unchanged.

**Open: position range.** The positions' conversion 64 + 31.5v fits an input
of −1 to 1. Live passes ExcitationX, ListeningXL and ListeningXR as 0–1 with
no remap (N5), so as traced they reach only from the centre to 0.72 of the
body. N5's evidence stops at Live's float parameter unit, which is inferred.
Probe P4-N5-01 should settle it.

## Module graph

Built in `0x5ca8`; each per-channel module exists twice, and the left instance
forwards every parameter message to the right.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    IN[Stereo input] --> PAN[DryWet panpot]
    PAN -->|wet| G[Gain] --> F[Band filter] --> R[ab_resonator x2]
    LFO[Stereo LFO] --> HUB[Pitch hub] -->|pitch, gate| R
    R --> W[Width crossfade] --> MIX[plus]
    PAN -->|dry| MIX --> OUT[Stereo output]
```

The engine processes sub-blocks of up to 512 samples and applies parameter
messages once per host block. The net output gain is unity.

## Resonator

**Types** (builders at `0x243e8`, `0x24ee4`, `0x25210` and `0x257b4`). Each
entry gives the ratios r_k:

| Live index | Internal | Model | Ratios r_k |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 1 Beam | modal | (β_k/4.730)²; β = 4.730, 7.853, 10.996, then (k+1.5)π |
| 1 | 2 Marimba | modal | β = 4.730, 9.413, 15.450, 20.710, 24.580, then (1.4142k+2.1213)π |
| 2 | 3 String | modal | k+1 |
| 3 | 4 Membrane | modal, 2-D | √(m²+(Rn)²)/√(1+R²), with R = Ratio |
| 4 | 5 Plate | modal, 2-D | (m²+(Rn)²)/(1+R²) |
| 5 | 7 Pipe | waveguide | — |
| 6 | 6 Tube | waveguide | — |

This confirms the label order that the Corpus demo had to assume. The Marimba
ratios start 1, 3.96, 10.67; Membrane at R = 1.5 starts 1, 1.387, 1.754.

**Modal model** (`0x1f3f8`):
- **Mode count.** Quality selects 4, 16, 30 or 70 modes. There is no
  oversampling.
- **Mode frequency.** Mode k's angular frequency is
  1643.807·2^p·r_k·r_k^(inh³), with pitch p in octaves.
- **Dropped modes.** A mode at or above 5/12 of the sample rate ends the list
  and turns Bleed off.
- **Damping.** Each mode is a two-pole resonator. Its damping is
  8·2^e / decay, where *e* tilts the damping by `tone` across the modes'
  log-ratios. Gain is tilted by `amp_freq`.
- **Hit and pickups.** Excitation and pickup weights come from a coarse
  mode-shape table with linear (1-D) or bilinear (2-D) interpolation, not from
  analytic sines. Each channel is mono: the left resonator listens at
  ListeningXL and the right at ListeningXR.
- **Update rate.** Coefficients update at most every 200 samples. Pickups move
  linearly over 4,000 samples.
- **Bleed.** A two-pole high-pass of the excitation is added before the ×3000
  output scale.

**Waveguide** (`0x23670`):
- **Lines.** Two 2,048-sample delay lines, each about fs/(2^p·523.24) − 0.75
  samples (half that for Tube). Reads use 5-tap Lagrange interpolation.
- **Feedback.** −0.999, with a 30 Hz DC blocker on the input.
- **Reflection.** A first-order reflection filter set by Radius and, for Pipe,
  Opening. Tube's loop is inverted once more.
- **Loss.** Per-trip loss is exp(−4/(decay·261.62·2^p)).

## The other modules

- **Panpot (DryWet).** The wet gain is P(a/4) and the dry gain P(0.25 − a/4),
  with P(t) = 6√3·t(1−t)(1−2t). Gains ramp over 100 samples.
- **Gain (Drive).** A linear gain of −15 to +15 dB with a 10 ms ramp. There is
  no saturation.
- **Band filter.** An RBJ low-pass at f·2^(bw/2) feeds an RBJ high-pass at
  f/2^(bw/2), both Q 0.707. Coefficients ramp over 30 samples, and on/off fades
  over 10 ms.
- **Width.** L' = (½+½w)L + (½−½w)R, applied to the resonated signal only.
- **LFO.** Seven shapes, in order: Sine (polynomial), Square, Triangle, Ramp
  Up, Ramp Down, Sample and Hold (phase at double rate), Random Ramp.
  - Free rate: 0.01·1000^(c/127) Hz. Sync uses a 22-entry bar table from 8 to
    1/64.
  - Stereo: Phase mode applies a fixed offset to the right channel; Spin mode
    runs the right channel faster.
  - Output adds to pitch: Amount 1 is ±1 octave.
- **Pitch hub.**
  - With MidiPitch off, pitch is the fixed pitch (from Frequency) plus the LFO,
    with Detune added on the left and subtracted on the right.
  - With MidiPitch on, the earlier report describes (note − 60)/12 plus bend,
    Fine and Transpose. Its highest-held-note shorthand is not a universal
    priority law: the [later bounded source query](#later-bounded-midi-pitch-evidence--2026-10-19)
    leaves arbitrary sustain/control histories and caller updates unresolved.
  - The gate is open unless MidiGate is on and no note is held.

## Quirks a faithful port reproduces

1. Resonator parameters move in 128 steps.
2. The integer driver maps controller 64 to 63: Transpose +16 sounds as +15.
3. Pitch and LFO changes reach the modal filters at most every 200 samples.
4. Pipe and Tube ring below their nominal pitch because the reflection filter
   adds delay. At 48 kHz with default Radius and Opening, the port gives
   251.0 Hz and 241.2 Hz against a nominal 261.62 Hz.
5. Bleed's minimum is 0.01, not 0.
6. Bleed turns off when any mode passes 5/12 of the sample rate.

# Device audio by extracted execution (T1.2 feasibility gate)

**Question.** Workstream T1.2 of [roadmap revision 3](native-decompilation-roadmap.md#revision-3--t1-completion-plan-2026-10-18)
starts with a gate. Can a harness load a device bundle's x86_64 slice, drive it the way Live does
and render audio? Are the renders deterministic and bit-for-bit repeatable? Can they be explained
by the static [Corpus DSP model](corpus-dsp-static.md)? Can the instrument path (note events in,
audio out) be driven? What metric should a device spec state, and what would the other five
devices need?

**Answer (X, draft). The gate passes.**

- **Loading.** A loader adapted from the [extracted-execution harness](extracted-execution.md)
  loads the Corpus, Analog, Tension, Collision and Electric slices. It creates instances and
  renders through the bundles' own `CalcA`. No exception path, fault or unbound import was hit.
- **Repeatability.** Corpus renders are bit-identical in these cases:
  - re-runs in new processes (6 of 6);
  - host blocks of 64, 256, 333 and 2,048 frames against 512, with constant parameters;
  - flush-to-zero and denormals-are-zero against the default MXCSR;
  - another clock value for the random seed, except where a random LFO shape is selected.
- **Static model.** Against the [static model](corpus-dsp-static.md) of the modal resonator:
  - mode frequencies agree within about one binary32 ulp of the mode's filter coefficients
    (41 impulse cases, both channels);
  - decay rates agree within about two ulps;
  - mode amplitudes, and with them the strike and pickup position effects, agree to 2.8 × 10⁻⁴
    (Membrane, with closely spaced modes, 2.3 × 10⁻³);
  - steady-state sine gains agree to 2.2 × 10⁻⁴ dB, and noise third-octave levels to 0.004 dB.
- **Port.** Every difference from the [traced port](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/demos/corpus-traced/index.html)
  is explained ([differences](#differences-and-their-explanations)).
- **Instrument path.** Analog plays notes from 16-byte events. Its note-on and note-off take effect
  on a 1 ms control grid, by an exact rule that holds for all 300 tested events.
- **Other devices.** Tension and Electric render notes after six more bindings. Collision runs, but
  its parameter path is not understood yet. Amp and Cabinet stop in a static initializer at
  `dladdr` and need a much larger macOS emulation ([effort](#effort-for-the-other-five-devices)).

## How Live drives a bundle

Live side (S, from [N5](device-parameter-mapping-native.md#how-live-loads-a-bundle)). Live
loads `<resources>/Devices/Mac/<Name>.bundle` and resolves the seven exports by name. It queries
`GetPlugInfoU`. It calls `CreateInstanceU()` and then `SetSampleRateU(handle, rate)` with the
current rate. Parameters are flushed as `SetParameterA(handle, index, value)` with the index
order and conversions of N5 and [N6](device-tables-native.md). The reviewed
[processing-protocol trace](device-host-protocol.md#initialization-reset-sample-rate-and-teardown)
distinguishes ordinary Reset/NewRate (no warm-up) from ResetAndDispatch: four
1,024-frame helper requests, then reset and cached index-0 restoration for the
reset-capable primary. This corrects the earlier one-warm-up shorthand; the
exact initialization/reset audio remains unknown. Live sets flush-to-zero around `SetSampleRateU`,
`SetParameterA` and `ResetA` (arm64).

Bundle side (X and S, x86_64 disassembly in this packet). The calling convention is System V.

| Export | Corpus x86_64 | Analog x86_64 | Arguments and result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CreateInstanceU` | `0x23b0` | `0x1fd70` | () → instance |
| `DestroyInstanceU` | `0x2460` | `0x1fdf0` | (instance) |
| `SetSampleRateU` | `0x2490` | `0x1fe60` | (instance, rate in Hz as a 64-bit integer) → 1 |
| `GetPlugInfoU` | `0x2930` | `0x1fed0` | (selector, out, size) → 1 if answered |
| `CalcA` | `0x29c0` | `0x1ff80` | (instance, frames, L, R, event count, events, transport, flag); the last two are stack arguments |
| `SetParameterA` | `0x2d60` | `0x20290` | (instance, index as int, value as float in `xmm0`) |
| `ResetA` | `0x2d80` | `0x20310` | (instance) |

The `CalcA` arguments that H4 and N5 left unknown, as the bundles read them:

- **Buffers.** `L` and `R` are processed in place: input in, output out.
- **Events.** 16 bytes each: a 64-bit frame offset, then status, data 1 and data 2 bytes. Corpus
  queues an event with frame − 1 when the frame is non-zero; Analog uses the frame as given.
- **Transport.** {int32 playing, padding, binary64 position, binary64 tempo}. Analog reads it
  unconditionally. Corpus accepts a null pointer.
- **Flag.** For Corpus, a non-zero `*flag` on entry means input is present; otherwise the engine
  reads silence. On return, Corpus clears it after fs/10 quiet frames (S). Analog writes 1 while
  it still sounds (X: 1 during the note, 0 after the release).
- **Block size.** `GetPlugInfoU` selector 5 answers 512 for both bundles. Corpus also processes
  internally in sub-blocks of at most 512 frames (S).

The selector answers measured (X) equal H4's static table.

**Not known (U).** Which frame base Live uses for events (0- or 1-based); what Live passes as the
transport and the input flag; Live's real block sizes; and when it runs the reset sequence.
The harness passes transport {0, 0.0, 120.0} and input flag 1 for effects (0 for instruments).

| `rand`, `srand` | The FreeBSD-lineage Park–Miller generator (16807, modulus 2³¹ − 1). This is inferred from Apple's libc lineage, not read from Apple's binary |
| `time` | Fixed at 0, or at `XDEV_TIME`. Both bundles seed `rand` with `srand(time(0))` while building their engines (Corpus `0x199c0`) |
| C++ ABI | `__dynamic_cast` and the three `__cxxabiv1` type_info vtables from libstdc++, which implements the same Itanium ABI. Exceptions, `__cxa_throw` and unwinding are trapped |
| libc++ (`std::__1`) | 59 members reimplemented in `xdev_cxx.c` on libc++'s x86_64 layouts: `std::string` standard layout (checked in the bundles' inline code), `ios_base`, `basic_ios`, `basic_streambuf` slots, `istream` (`get`, `unget`, `putback`, `tellg`, `seekg`, `>>` int and unsigned), `ostream` (`<<` int, unsigned long, bool, float, double; `put`, `flush`), the sentries, `locale` and `ctype<char>` |

The bundles need the stream shim. Corpus builds its module graph from text written to
`ostringstream`s and parsed with `sscanf`. It constructs its engine state from an embedded text
patch read through an `istringstream`. On every sample-rate change it saves that state through a
`stringstream` and reads it back. Floats are written with libc++'s default `%.*g`, precision 6,
and read back with `atof`. A traced rate change (`XDEV_TRACE_OSTREAM`) wrote 51 floats, all at
precision 6. No stream extraction set the fail bit (`cxx-failbits 0` in every log).

### Differences and their explanations

1. **Start-up.** The port ramps the panpot gains from frame 0. The original is silent for the
   first 100 frames and then ramps over the next 100. This explains the port's 4–11 % error on
   inputs that start at frame 0. The report's "both gains start at 0" is right, but it leaves out
   that the first ramp starts only after 100 frames.
2. **Precision.** The port computes the coefficients in binary64. The original computes and
   stores them in binary32. Low modes are the most sensitive, and their phase drifts: rel RMS
   4 × 10⁻² at 66 Hz. The static model with binary32 rounding is within one ulp bound.
3. **Pipe and Tube pitch.** [Corpus DSP](corpus-dsp-static.md#quirks-a-faithful-port-reproduces)
   quirk 4 and CD-C07 give 251.0 Hz and 241.2 Hz at 48 kHz. X and the port both give 251.271
   and 241.687 Hz; the page's figures were rough readings. The drops are 3.96 % and 7.62 %, as
   CD-C07 says ("about 4 % and 8 %").
4. **Sample-rate change.** Not in the static model: the six-digit state round trip
   ([determinism](#determinism)).
5. **DecayOnNoteOff.** The port passes the stored value through the D rule. Live sends 1 − v
   (N5). It matters only while MidiGate closes the gate, which no case exercised.
6. **Random LFO shapes.** These are seeded from the clock in the original and from `Math.random`
   in the port. Neither can be compared sample by sample.

No difference between X and the static model remains unexplained.

## Signal preparation and host mixing

`0x102fc0e2c` (record 39) chooses instrument processing for input-role 1 and
an effect path for role 2. H4/N5 establish instrument/effect applicability.
`0x102fc070c` (37) copies both source channels into the effect's working output
buffers when both input pointers exist, otherwise zeros both. Its initial activity
flag is **input presence**, not a scan for nonzero samples. Therefore a supplied
all-zero stereo buffer and absent input are different boundary inputs. Instruments
instead initialize the flag from queued-event count; their working output is not
filled from the audio input on this branch. In-place buffers alone do not imply
that a stopped effect is always called.

Amp/Cabinet's dual-instance capability selects `0x102fc0294` (35) when DualMono
is enabled: independent left and right processing with the same event/transport
context; activity is ORed. Disabled DualMono uses `0x102fc04dc` (36): the wet input
is `(L+R)/2`, processed once, then used for both wet channels. Original dry stereo
remains available to the mix. The flag still reflects both inputs being present.
This establishes signal preparation; it supplies no Amp/Cabinet DSP output.

Those two paths call `0x101df082c` (7) for host dry/wet mixing. At a settled control
value d, wet weight is `sin(d*pi/2)` and dry weight is
`sqrt(1-wet_weight^2)`, with separate original L/R dry samples. The transition uses
an iterative update and a 0.001 control step per sample; do not substitute a
linear crossfade or claim a sample-exact transition from this draft. N5 owns how
stored DryWet reaches this control; `OnDryWet` (49) forwards into its setter.
Corpus's own DryWet is a bundle parameter, not this Amp/Cabinet host crossfade.

## Parameter delivery and processing boundaries

`OnParameter` (45; duplicate body 30) stores the last value for each index and
records first-seen index order. An entry is accepted only with an existing primary
instance, index below 256 and fewer than 256 distinct pending entries. At full
capacity even a repeated index is ignored because the count guard precedes lookup.
`0x102fbfe54` (32) delivers that order to primary and any secondary instance, then
clears the pending entries/count. For the reset-capable group it also remembers
index 0. These are queue observations, not a claim that UI automation is sampled
only once per audio block.

`0x102fc0a38` (38) normally flushes before processing. For the reset-capable group,
more than 10 pending distinct values instead select a grouped-change path; active
processing starts a fade of `int(0.03 * sample_rate)` frames, otherwise dispatch
begins immediately. `0x102fbf9a0` (27) transfers pending values into another queue,
disables processing and posts reset/dispatch work. Resume handlers (19/21) re-enable
or repeat the sequence. Scheduler timing, observed interruption duration and
which user edits cross this threshold remain unknown. No compatibility requirement
requires a 10-entry queue, fade implementation or original call sequence.

## Events and partitioning

`0x102fbfb5c` (28), gated by readiness and device On, accepts logical event types
1/2/6, and type 3 with controller code -2, -1, 1, 64, 74 or 120. The bit mask is
`0x100000000000401` after subtracting 64. Other logical types/codes are not queued
by this path. Queue capacity is 4,096 events; subsequent arrivals are ignored.
Accepted events trigger processing activity. These are logical-event filter
observations, not a claim that MIDI transformations before this path are absent.

The queue uses `0x101ab4ee4` (4) → `0x101a541a4` (2) for the current scheduler offset
and `0x101b4456c` (5) for MIDI-byte conversion. Notes use note-on/note-off status
with channel nibble, pitch byte and converted velocity; type 6 becomes CC123=0.
The scheduler offset's origin is **unknown**: neither this getter nor copying it
establishes whether Live's event coordinate starts at 0 or 1. This packet does
not settle fractional velocity rounding across the whole event path, MPE, channel
remapping or Corpus's MIDI side-chain routing.

When a processing request exceeds the capability maximum, `0x102fbe73c` (13) and
inline copies choose a split helper `0x102fbe964` (15). For a supported request of
1,024 frames with a 512-frame maximum, the helper processes two subblocks. Events
strictly before each subblock end are copied and their timestamp is reduced by
that subblock's start. Thus event coordinate 512 belongs to the second subblock
at 0; 511 belongs to the first at 511. This translation preserves coordinates;
it does not determine their original time base. The local event limit is 2,048
per subblock; overflow behavior is incompletely characterized because the source
cursor advances past the entire selected range. Events must already be ordered
for the binary search to be meaningful; upstream ordering was not proved.

The caller calculates a quotient `frames / maximum`; no remainder path is present
in the exported split helper. Its decompile has stack-probe recovery. Therefore
non-multiple request sizes, zero maximum and invalid sizes remain **U**, not an
inferred claim that Live drops audio. The real scheduler may constrain requests;
this packet has not established that constraint.

## Transport context

The pre-buffer callback `0x102fcce00` (50) copies playing state, position and tempo
from scheduler status; tempo is converted binary32→binary64. It also supplies loop
start/end and loop-enabled state. Field semantics follow the bundle-side context
in the DSP study, but the scheduler status producer is not fully traced.

For each split subblock, record 15 leaves position unchanged while stopped. While
playing it advances position by `tempo * start_frame / (sample_rate * 60)`.
**Inferred unit:** quarter-note beats, consistent with the formula; no independent
scheduler-unit proof is retained here. If looping is enabled and the subblock
advance crosses the copied loop end, a helper adjusts the position. Its exact
boundary/modulo rule is **U**. Non-normative numeric model vectors below deliberately
avoid loop crossings. No wall-clock, tempo-change or transport-jump latency follows.

## Initialization, reset, sample rate and teardown

Initialization and loading remain owned by N5. This packet adds:

- `NewRate` (31/44): if a primary exists, temporarily disables readiness, stores
  the new rate in primary and secondary, delivers rate updates to both, resets
  both, re-delivers cached index 0 to the primary for the reset-capable group,
  clears queued events and restores prior readiness. Return values of rate/reset
  calls are not used here. Which notes are re-sent by upstream scheduling is U.
- Ordinary `Reset` (26/42): resets primary and secondary and restores cached
  index 0 for the reset-capable primary. **No warm-up is called on this path.**
- `ResetAndDispatch` (18→20): flushes the transferred parameters; for reset-capable
  engines calls `0x102fbff98` **four times**, first with an event, next three with
  no events; then resets primary, re-delivers index 0 and resets secondary.
  Each warm-up helper invocation requests 1,024 frames (33), split into two
  512-frame calls for the five non-Softube devices. Total is therefore 4,096
  warm-up frames on this path, not 1,024. Its synthetic event constructor (6)
  is retained, but its exact semantic identity is not assigned here.
- `Exit` (25/41) disables readiness, marks exit and unregisters pre/post callbacks.
  The destructor (24) destroys each extant engine, frees its wrapper and decrements
  the shared loader count. When it reaches zero `0x102f999fc` (8) clears export
  pointers and releases the CFBundle. This is static resource teardown, not proof
  of a particular device-delete sound or UI timing.

new-rate/reset renders and grouped-change renders remain ungraded until separately
supported. Root integration owns the backlinks/correction notices in N5 and the

The call wrapper (14) converts a boolean input flag to an integer for processing,

# Corpus audio effect: signal behavior and reference renders

## Scope

Feature FEAT-DEVICES, T1 device audio ([ADR 0004](../decisions/adr-0004-target-scope-t1.md)).
User task: a track holds the bundled Corpus effect, and the offline render of that track
must sound as Live's would. This draft specifies:

- the output Corpus produces for a stereo input and a set of stored parameter values, at
  44.1 kHz and 48 kHz;
- the reference renders that define that output for T1, and the protocol that made them;
- the comparison metric a candidate render must meet.

How the parameters are stored, with their domains and defaults, is
[SPEC-BUNDLED-DEVICE-PARAMETERS](bundled-device-parameters.md). Where Corpus sits in the
track's signal flow belongs to the mix-graph and playback specs.

Excluded:

- MIDI side-chain behavior beyond the two exact extracted held-note host-input cases
  DCO-030 and DCO-031: general MidiPitch, MidiGate, Transpose, FineTranspose,
  PitchBendRange, DecayOnNoteOff, MidiMode and Live side-chain routing remain U
  (REQ-013). The two cases define finite bundle outputs, not Live routing;
- LFO Sync and the random LFO shapes as exact waveforms (REQ-011);
- parameter automation during a render beyond the timing rules of REQ-012;
- display text, CPU load and latency reporting.

Every requirement is a **proposed contract**. Nothing was run against Live, and under
[ADR 0003](../decisions/adr-0003-no-reference-execution.md) nothing will be. The audio
evidence is extracted execution of the shipped x86_64 Corpus code. The Live-side
parameter path is a static derivation. Canonical evidence:
[device DSP by extracted execution](../research/device-dsp-extracted.md).

## Evidence labels

| Label | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| D | Documented in shipped bytes: the schema, the shipped presets and the bundle's export table |
| S | Static derivation from the 12.4.3 executables; not an observed run |

It shows what the device code computes for those calls. It does not show that Live makes the same calls. The arm64 release slice is matched only by static comparison (appendix) |

## Assumptions

| ID | Assumption | What rests on it |

| A1 | Live passes the stored ExcitationX, ListeningXL and ListeningXR values (0..1) to the device unchanged, as its float parameter unit is traced to do for every other identity-mapped Corpus parameter. Static route: trace the value that unit emits | REQ-002, REQ-008; cases DCO-013, 014 and 028 for stored values |
| A2 | The device sees the protocol of REQ-001. That is: the sample rate is set before the parameters; all 38 values are sent; transport not playing; input flagged as present. Live's call order is static (S); the transport and flag values Live passes are unknown | REQ-001, every case |

## Requirements

### REQ-DEVICE-CORPUS-001 — reference renders define the output

- **X.** For T1, Corpus's output for an input and a set of host values is the reference render
  made with this protocol:
  1. a new instance is created;
  2. the sample rate is set (44,100 or 48,000 Hz);
  3. all 38 host values of REQ-002 are sent, in index order;
  4. processing starts at the first frame, in host blocks of 512 frames;
  5. the input is stereo binary32, flagged as present;
  6. the transport is not playing (position 0, 120 BPM).

  The reference renders are retained with their inputs and SHA-256 (cases below). The
  output is stereo binary32, one output frame for each input frame.
- **X; proposed finite engineering scope.** DCO-030 and DCO-031 use the complete
  38-value host vector and event fixture below: new instance, 44,100 Hz, parameters
  in index order, one held note-on at absolute host/test frame1537, then one
  16,384-frame process in blocks512 with I1 at4096. The only difference between
  those two histories is key60 versus72. MidiPitch=1 and MidiGate=0; LFO is off.
  Stopped transport is `{playing:0, position:0, tempo:120}` and is not advanced;
  input flag1, MXCSR0x1f80 and time seed0 characterize the reference calls.

  occurs. The event has status0x90, channel0 and velocity100, and remains held
  through destruction. The canonical input coordinate is1537 (block1536/local1);
  do not subtract again in an adapter. Live's event base and actual delivery are U.

  - the clock value with which the device seeds its random generator, except for the random
    LFO shapes (REQ-011).

  Re-running a case gives a bit-identical render.
- **S, X.** Live creates the instance, sets the current sample rate and sends the parameter values

| --- | --- | --- |

in each denominator coefficient moves a low mode's frequency by up to 3·2⁻²⁵/θ² relative.

- one-ulp changes of the substituted libm results move a 66 Hz mode by 6.8 × 10⁻⁴ and change

- the arm64 release slice has 232 fused multiply-adds that the x86_64 slice lacks.

spaced modes limit the estimator, and the margin there is about two. On paths that do not
resonate the effects are 10⁻⁵ or smaller, so a waveform tolerance can be used there.
